g.title: CIPN_QSP
g.text: Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (CIPN) — Mechanistic QSP Map
Neurotoxic Drug Exposure (Cmax vs AUC vs Cumulative Dose) → DRG / Distal Axon Injury → Committed Degeneration & Coasting → Hyperexcitability → CIPN20 / TNSc / Dose Intensity / Tumour Control

g.title: cluster_drugs
g.text: 1. Neurotoxic Chemotherapy: Class, Schedule & Cumulative Dose (the exposure the whole model is driven by)

g.title: cluster_transport
g.text: 3. Why the DRG? Transporters & the Absent Blood–Nerve Barrier (the anatomical basis of selectivity)

g.title: cluster_platinum
g.text: 4. Platinum Mechanism: Nuclear & Mitochondrial DNA Adducts in the Post-Mitotic Neuron

g.title: cluster_microtubule
g.text: 5. Microtubule & Axonal Transport Failure (taxanes, vinca alkaloids, auristatin ADCs)

g.title: cluster_mito
g.text: 7. Mitochondrial Dysfunction & Oxidative Stress (the shared convergence node of all classes)

g.title: cluster_degeneration
g.text: 8. Committed Degeneration & COASTING (why CIPN worsens for weeks AFTER the last dose)

g.title: cluster_channels
g.text: 9. Ion-Channel Remodelling & Peripheral Hyperexcitability (fast, reversible — the ACUTE syndrome)

g.title: cluster_neuroinflam
g.text: 10. Peripheral Neuroinflammation (DRG macrophages, satellite glia, Schwann cells, mast cells)

g.title: cluster_central
g.text: 11. Spinal Dorsal Horn & Descending Modulation (central amplification — the duloxetine target)

g.title: cluster_risk
g.text: 12. Host Risk Modifiers & Pharmacogenomics (why identical exposure gives different CIPN)

g.title: cluster_prevention
g.text: 13. Prevention: Exposure-Limiting Strategies (must be applied AT EVERY infusion to work)

g.title: cluster_treatment
g.text: 14. Symptomatic Treatment PK/PD (treats the SYMPTOM, not the axon)

g.text: 16. The Dose-Intensity Dilemma (every neuroprotective dose reduction is also an anti-tumour dose reduction)
